video_goal: Demonstrate the visual process of assembling, molding, and finishing a traditional Cantonese-style mooncake.
required_subjects_and_props: Golden syrup dough, lotus seed paste, salted duck egg yolks, flour, spring-loaded mooncake mold, baking sheet, spray bottle, pastry brush, egg wash, knife.

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands knead a shiny, amber-colored golden syrup dough inside a clear glass bowl until it forms a smooth ball.
Fingers flatten a scoop of smooth, brown lotus seed paste and wrap it completely around a bright orange salted duck egg yolk.
Hands roll the lotus paste and egg yolk mixture between the palms into a perfectly smooth, round ball.
Thumbs press a small portion of the golden syrup dough into a thin, flat circular disc on a lightly floured wooden board.
Hands place the lotus paste ball into the center of the dough disc and gently push the dough edges upward to encase the filling.
Fingers pinch the top of the dough closed, then roll the entire stuffed ball between the palms until the seam disappears.
Hands lightly roll the stuffed dough ball in a shallow dish of white flour, then tap it gently to shake off the excess.
Hands insert the floured dough ball into the open cavity of a spring-loaded plastic mooncake mold featuring an intricate floral pattern plate.
Hands press the mold firmly down onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, holding the top plunger handle down steadily for two seconds.
The hand lifts the mold handle, releasing a perfectly shaped raw mooncake with sharp, raised Chinese characters and floral designs on its surface.
A plastic spray bottle mists a fine layer of water over the raw, shaped mooncake resting on the baking sheet.
A soft pastry brush lightly dabs a shiny golden egg yolk wash exclusively over the raised patterns of the partially baked mooncake.
A knife slices the glossy, baked golden-brown mooncake in half, pulling the halves apart to reveal the centered orange egg yolk surrounded by lotus paste.
